sentences.text: The Williamson turn brings you back down your own track, which makes it the best choice at night or when you’ve lost sight of the person.
Put the rudder hard over toward the side the person fell from.
When you’re about sixty degrees off your original course, shift the rudder hard over the other way.
Steady up on the reciprocal of your original course, and you’ll be running back down your track toward the person.
When the person is in sight and close, a quicker single turn, like the Anderson turn, brings you back faster.
